Ghana e-waste images: what the data says

GIZ Data Lab E-Waste Hackathon · Track 2 (Data Visualization & Insights) · Yalem Tilahun. Built from the open scrapyard photo collection and its labels (CC-BY-4.0).

Key findings

  • 4,301 photos were audited; 100% were readable. Filename-based capture dates range from 22 May 2025 to 27 Oct 2025, across 44 capture sessions. The dataset cards describe the collection as October 2025; 39 photos carry earlier filename dates.
  • 689 photos (16%) have boxes, with 1,682 boxes in total. Category statistics therefore describe the labelled subset, not the entire photo collection.
  • ACs is the largest category (16% of boxes), and the top three categories account for 46%. The smallest category is unsure (1.1%).
  • 1.1% of boxes are labelled 'unsure', meaning the annotators could not decide on a category.
  • Cooling equipment (ACs, Fridges and Compressors) represents 42% of all boxes. These are visible-item counts, not weight or material quantities.
  • 18% of labelled photos contain no box. These images can be useful as negative or context examples, but they do not contribute to category counts.
  • 2% of shots are flagged as near-duplicates under the defined time-and-hash rule. For future modelling, splits should use capture sessions rather than random image-level splitting to reduce leakage risk.
  • 8% of photos are flagged for review: blurry 8%, too dark 0%, too bright 0%, flat contrast 0%. These are heuristics and should be checked in the gallery.
  • 2,428 photos carry GPS metadata.

What we recommend

  1. Show label coverage next to every category statistic so the labelled subset is not mistaken for the whole collection.
  2. For future modelling, split data by capture session and remove or down-weight near-duplicates before evaluating models.
  3. Add more labels for rare categories and review 'unsure' boxes before using them for model training.
  4. Record site and date metadata separately from filenames so the collection can support analysis by place and season.
  5. Reconcile the category list with the dataset description, including the 'mixed scraps' concept where appropriate; do not invent a class that is absent from the labels.

Method, limits and sources

  • Photos: GIZ/E-Waste-Database. Each photo is opened once and shrunk to 768 px before measuring, so sharpness is comparable across phones.
  • Labels: COCO json from GIZ/e-waste-dataset-COCO-labels, cross-checked against GIZ/e-waste-dataset-yolo-labels. Stray records outside the release were dropped.
  • Capture time comes from file names (IMG_/PXL_ timestamps). A capture stop ends after a pause of over 5 minutes. A near-duplicate is a shot less than 10 seconds after the previous one with a similar 64-bit fingerprint.
  • Quality flags are heuristics (blur is relative to this collection), not ground truth. Categories are the labellers' choice and include "unsure". Box counts are items, not weight.
Data dictionary and reuse

image_audit.csv (one row per photo): file, width/height (pixels as displayed), megapixels, file_mb, brightness (0-255 average), contrast (spread of grey values), sharpness (Laplacian variance at 768 px), dark_share / bright_share (share of pure black / white pixels), photo_hash, has_gps, camera_model, taken (from the file name), capture_stop, near_duplicate, blurry / too_dark / too_bright / flat, needs_review, labelled, n_boxes.
labels_clean.csv (one row per box): file, category, x / y / box_width / box_height (pixels, top-left origin), area_share, out_of_frame.
